thread:
maria_cust: Hey team — we started getting a flood of 429s in production around 09:34 UTC. Mostly on POST /v1/generate. Users hitting errors in spikes, lasts for ~20s then quiet.
deploy-bot: deploy finished 09:29 UTC -> release/patch-3.4.1 (no schema changes). :white_check_mark:
ingest-bot: anomaly detected: 09:34:12 - elevated request rate from customer_id=acme-ops, ~980 req/min over 1min window
alice_support: thanks, maria. Can you paste one full failing response (headers + body) and a sample request id? Also which SDK/version?
maria_cust: sample below. SDK 1.3.0. request id `req_0a9c3b`
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
Retry-After: 15
X-Rate-Limit-RPM: 60
X-Rate-Limit-Remaining: 0
X-Rate-Limit-TPM: 120000
X-Rate-Limit-Token-Remaining: 0
{
  "error": "Rate limit exceeded",
  "request_id": "req_0a9c3b"
}
```
lee_sre: RPM of 60 + TPM of 120k looks small vs their usage pattern. But the key clue is the spike shape — suggests many small requests aligning at a boundary. Do they use a heartbeat/polling pattern?
maria_cust: yes — client has a keepalive/heartbeat every 3s to check for updates, plus producers fanout to multiple worker threads. Each event triggers a short /generate call.
edge_engineer: that pattern will produce a LOT of tiny requests and if many clients align (cron-ish) you get minute-boundary bunching. Could be client clock drift syncing heartbeats after restart.
alice_support: two quick asks: 1) can you share server-side timestamps for those request_ids (we need the per-second arrival distribution) 2) can you try reproducing with a local script to confirm alignment?
maria_cust: grabbing logs now. here's a tiny repro script we used (python -> bash one-liner):
```
# simulate 200 clients all hitting at same second
for i in $(seq 1 200); do
  (sleep 0; curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"prompt":"x"}') &
done
wait
```
lee_sre: that will definitely show the same. Two mitigation paths: short-term (customer-side): add random jitter to heartbeat (0-10s), reduce per-client concurrency, aggregate small events into batch calls. Server-side options: temporary quota bump for 24h, or configure them on Dedicated/Reserved capacity for predictable throughput.
pm_jordan: noted, we can approve a +3x RPM temporary bump for acme-ops for 24h while they patch. Approving now.
alice_support: immediate action we recommended to customer: 1) enable jitter and exponential backoff w/ full jitter on retries, 2) cap concurrent SDK streams to 4, 3) change heartbeat interval from 3s -> 30s and add random +/-5s, 4) if they need steady low latency at scale, request Dedicated.
maria_cust: applied SDK change and jitter, throttled concurrency to 5. initial results: spike magnitude down ~80% on first test. Still seeing occasional 429 bursts on minute rollover.
lee_sre: still seeing minute-rollover bounces means some processes still synchronized. Next: ask them to stagger restart times and ensure long-lived connections (reduce reconnects). We'll also check edge layer aggregation settings.
edge_engineer: investigating edge logs — seeing many TCP connections tearing/reattaching at 09:33:58 -> that explains synchronized request flurry. If client reconnects then immediately does heartbeat, you get alignment. Recommend adding a randomized jitter on client reconnect too.
alice_support: I'm sending the temporary quota bump details and mitigation checklist to maria_cust. Also scheduling a 1:1 with their infra lead to walk through batching and Dedicated options.
maria_cust: thanks — acceptance test shows 90% reduction when staggering restarts + SDK jitter. We'll keep the temporary bump until EOD while we deploy patch. Appreciate the quick help! :pray:
lee_sre: follow-ups for us: collect sample arrival histogram + edge conn lifecycle logs for the 09:34 window, and propose an internal KB about "heartbeat-induced rate storms" with reproduction steps and common mitigations.
alice_support: adding KB draft to docs queue, will ping you both to review. Closing this thread after verification tomorrow unless customer reopens.
